plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In such auctions, bidding my true value is the weakly dominant strategy: bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win, and bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $14, I should bid exactly $14 to maximize expected profit without unnecessary risk.

This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above or below my value only risks either overpaying (if bid too high and forced to pay more than value in edge cases) or losing profitable auctions (if bid too low). Bidding exactly my value of $34 ensures I win whenever profitable and never pay more than the item is worth to me.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding exactly my value ensures I never overpay and capture all available surplus when I have the highest value. Bidding higher risks negative profit if I win at a price above my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $33.
